title: Montevideo, Rotterdam
status: reference evidence for original procedural reconstruction; fidelity review pending

facts: Interlocking volumes include a cantilever above the quay.
Steel lower two floors, concrete middle structure approximately 90 m high, steel upper structure.
Different floor heights and more than 50 apartment layouts; do not assume a uniform facade.
The M is an 8 m weather vane.
references.imageCredit: Ossip Architectuurfotografie and Christian Richters, as listed on the project page. References inspected in browser; no images downloaded or redistributed.

facts: The 2015 retrospective describes brick, roof terraces, loggias and varied window types, including circular openings.
Describes 44 floors, which conflicts with the 43-level map/catalog convention.
Concrete through floor 27, with steel above; ground and first two levels use columns/core/braces.
Upper three floors form a penthouse with a pool.
Steel diagonals behind the facade form the upper structural tube.
references.access: Search-indexed primary page text inspected; direct web open returned verification screen, but the normal browser navigation loaded the complete page without any challenge interaction.
references.drawingNotes: Inspected engineer's concept section: three structural zones, upper facade diagonals, cantilevered low wing and lower braced frame. Sketch labels the top 135 m+, so do not treat it as an as-built height schedule. Image is 752×838 pixels.

facts: Braced steel/concrete-filled columns below; 26 floors of concrete walls above; open steel structure from floor 28.
Quay wall and nearby Hotel New York constrained foundations.

facts: The article explicitly identifies an unserved mechanical transition floor named 27A; avoid treating all facade levels as one repeating interval.
Fifteen upper floors (29–43 in the article's construction count) use an open steel frame.
The M is 8 m high, 9 tonnes and reaches 152.317 m.
The lower roof water-tank sculpture is credited to Ineke Hauer.

Second-floor connection detail marks +8.020 m and +7.470 m, with a 600 mm square column and 600 mm brace. These datums are shown relative to an unstated project zero; confirm ground reference before use.
references.planNotes: Printed page 29 gives fifth- and thirtieth-floor plans, including a 0–20 m scale. The lower plan agrees with the measured long, stepped footprint. The upper floor has separate west and south steps. Its page origin and scale must be aligned independently; do not assume the two drawings share a coordinate origin or derive the upper tower by extruding the ground outline.
references.unavailableRelatedPublication: The publisher's free 2006 project-document URL returned HTTP 404; this is the original eight-page 2005 article, not that later publication.

facts: Architectural and tip height 152.3 m; highest occupied floor 133.4 m.

survey.axis: Native +X points northeast along the quay, +Z southeast toward the water. Tall tower occupies the negative-X end, low projecting wing the positive-X end. This is a working interpretation, pending overlay review.

remaining: Section has now been inspected at native resolution, but exact floor spacing and ground datum remain to establish; floor-count conventions differ and the extra 27A floor is explicit in the engineer's article.
Derive each volume from roof envelopes and compare upper cantilever footprint with photographs; BAG ground outline alone is insufficient and may include projected overhangs.

Record regular and alternating window modules separately for all four elevations, including white panel joints, loggias and circular openings. The original-architect upper western photograph shows fifteen stacked glazed balcony bands inside the brick frame; the pale wing has a distinct window field and the circular openings belong to lower levels.

The pale facade finish is visually established, but its material composition is not yet confirmed by a primary specification. Do not describe it as aluminium solely from photographs; supplier search hits for Montevideo in Antwerp concern a different building.
Resolve 139.5 m secondary roof-height claim against architect drawings and measured envelope rather than silently treating the 152.3 m tip as roof height.
Original source geometry and runtime import now exist. Current capture integrity, maximum fidelity and actual terrain placement are tracked separately in qa.json.

mediumFiReview.signedPlacement: Native+X east-northeast follows the AntoinePlatekade edge and native+Z south-southeast faces the Rijnhaven. Actual north-up Google satellite viewed2026-10-09 shows tall tower at the southwest negative-X end, lower projecting wing at the northeast positive-X end, terraces between and quay on the southeast. Architect river overview and cantilever photograph independently show that signed arrangement. The glass-fronted low-wing cantilever remains open below over the pedestrian quay; the BAG perimeter is an upper-volume projection, not a ground solid. RD-to-WGS84 operation accuracy1m and approximately3degree heading uncertainty describe reconstructed placement, not a surveyed azimuth.
mediumFiReview.scope: Static medium-fi exterior preserves the unchanged original493066-triangle detailed draft and supplies a separate reviewed terracotta-soffit source correction with four complete browser levels. Published152.317m tip and8m weather vane are retained, with a fixed documented M pose. Three structural zones, offset brick/pale volumes, circular windows, recessed glazed loggias, connecting terraces, braced open quay cantilever, roof tank sculpture and parked crane are retained. Exact43/44floor conventions,27A technical floor, individual floor heights, pale-panel substrate, balcony depths, entrance details and roof equipment proportions remain reconstructed. 2022BAG roof envelope has2.20mRMSE. GroundNAP3.279 is estimated, not surveyed. Hidden interiors, underground parking, adjoining buildings, vessels and surrounding quay are excluded; real host pavement/quay fitting is required and footprint replacement is disabled.
